products.skip: P1 — no exon skipped; ASO-mediated EXCLUSION of the putative NMD-inducing exon ('exon 16x') in CDKL5 intron 16, from the patient's non-mutant allele
products.natural_human_equivalent: Product is the wild-type 960-aa brain isoform, so the human equivalent is any healthy CDKL5 allele. Dose-level equivalent: females with favourably skewed X-inactivation and post-zygotic mosaics, who are mild or unaffected — natural proof that raising canonical CDKL5 per neuron is sufficient. Upper bound exists: CDKL5 duplication carriers show autism, DD, macrocephaly without epilepsy (search snippet, full text not verified).
products.domain_consequence: None. No coding sequence altered: kinase domain 13-297, ATP site 19-27/42, catalytic D135 and the entire C-terminal regulatory/NLS-NES region are intact; output is the canonical brain isoform.
products.rescue_evidence: No CDKL5-specific ASO data found, published or in a pipeline. The only CDKL5 citation for this event is a Stoke patent naming 'exon 16x' in intron 16 with no supporting expression data. Indirect: adult re-expression of Cdkl5 at the endogenous locus in mice reverses most behavioural and NMDAR deficits (working memory not reversible). Searches tried: PubMed 'CDKL5 ASO poison exon', 'CDKL5 NMD exon', EuropePMC 'CDKL5 antisense oligonucleotide' (503), web 'CDKL5 TANGO 2025', 'Stoke CDKL5 pipeline'.
products.why: The product itself is perfect — unmodified canonical protein from the healthy allele — but the enabling non-productive splicing event is asserted only in a data-free patent, so existence and magnitude in human neurons are unverified.

findings.claim: CDKL5 kinase domain spans aa 13-297; ATP binding 19-27 and 42; active site D135; 960-aa sequence with a brain-predominant alternative C-terminus (905-960).
Patent WO2019084050A1 names an NMD-inducing exon 'exon 16x' within CDKL5 intron 16 and ASO targeting regions, but presents no CDKL5 expression data.
Favourable X-inactivation skewing or post-zygotic mosaicism can yield mild or unaffected CDKL5 carriers.
Adult restoration of CDKL5 in mice improved hyperactivity, anxiety and motor deficits and normalised EB2 Ser222 phosphorylation; working memory deficits were not reversible.

products.skip: P2 — no exon skipped; ASO redirection away from 3'-terminal non-productive CDKL5 isoforms (exon-20-containing transcripts whose frame stops near the end of exon 20) toward hCDKL5_1
products.natural_human_equivalent: Same as P1 — the product is the canonical 960-aa hCDKL5_1 brain protein. The non-productive isoform being suppressed is itself a normal constituent of human brain RNA, so its reduction has no truncated-protein equivalent to phenotype.
products.domain_consequence: None. Coding sequence unchanged; shifting isoform usage toward hCDKL5_1 (18 exons, 6.6 kb 3'UTR), the predominant human brain transcript.
products.rescue_evidence: None found for CDKL5. Event is described in human/mouse transcript characterisation: exon 20 inclusion terminates the frame near the end of exon 20 with splicing detected downstream. No ASO has been applied to it. Same search set as P1.
products.why: Identical ideal product to P1 but the non-productive splicing event is at least documented in real human brain transcript data rather than only in a patent.

findings.claim: The predominant human brain CDKL5 transcript hCDKL5_1 is a 9.7 kb, 18-exon mRNA with a 6.6 kb 3'UTR; multiple novel splice and UTR isoforms exist with tissue- and developmental-stage-specific expression.
Inclusion of CDKL5 exon 20 gives a frame terminating near the end of exon 20, with splicing detected after that exon (3'-end RNA-seq reads in brain and testis).

products.skip: P9 — no exon skipped; ASO targeting the 6.6 kb CDKL5 3'UTR / uORF to raise translation or stability of the existing canonical mRNA
products.natural_human_equivalent: Product is canonical 960-aa protein; equivalent is the normal allele. Dosage equivalent again the mildly-affected skewed-XCI females; ceiling set by duplication carriers.
products.domain_consequence: None — no change to the coding sequence or to any domain.
products.rescue_evidence: None found for CDKL5. GeneReviews notes pathogenic variants in a 170-nt noncoding 3' region of the brain transcript, confirming the 3' end is functionally regulatory, but no ASO upregulation data exist. Searches: web 'CDKL5 3'UTR ASO upregulation', PubMed CDKL5 isoform/3'UTR.
products.why: Perfect product, but no CDKL5 3'UTR regulatory element has been mapped to an ASO-actionable repressor, so there is currently no design handle.

findings.claim: Pathogenic CDKL5 variants occur in a 170-nucleotide noncoding 3' region of the predominant brain transcript, historically missed by clinical labs.
hCDKL5_1 carries a 6.6 kb 3'UTR, a large regulatory surface.

products.skip: P4 — no exon skipped as therapy; ASO/ExSpeU1 restoration of canonical exon inclusion for a splice-site allele (e.g. c.2376+5G>A, which causes exon 16 skipping and NMD)
products.natural_human_equivalent: Product is the canonical full-length protein restored from the patient's own mutant allele. Untreated equivalent: carriers of c.2376+1/+5 variants, who have classic CDD with ~80% reduction in CDKL5 protein in lymphocytes.
products.domain_consequence: None in the rescued transcript — exon 16 inclusion is restored, avoiding the frameshift and premature stop in exon 18; kinase domain 13-297 and C-terminal region intact.
products.rescue_evidence: Direct and quantitative: ExSpeU1 constructs restored >70% CDKL5 protein for the +5 model with dose-dependent recovery of kinase activity, in HEK293T, SH-SY5Y, patient lymphoblastoid cells (c.2376+5G>A) and Cdkl5-null hippocampal neurons. Critically, only +5 variants were rescuable; +1 canonical-site variants were not.
products.why: Strongest direct CDKL5 rescue data of any option and restores the true canonical protein, but it only serves the small splice-variant subgroup and the modality demonstrated was U1 snRNA, not an ASO.

findings.claim: CDKL5 c.2376+5G>A causes exon 16 skipping, frameshift and a premature stop in exon 18 leading to NMD; patient lymphocytes showed ~80% reduction in CDKL5 protein.
ExSpeU1 restored >70% of CDKL5 protein and dose-dependent kinase activity for +5 splice variants, but failed to rescue +1 canonical splice-site variants.

products.skip: P5 — no exon skipped; Xist-targeting ASO (± DNMT inhibitor) to reactivate the wild-type CDKL5 allele on the inactive X in females
products.natural_human_equivalent: Product is canonical CDKL5 from the silenced wild-type allele. Human equivalent is precisely the favourably-skewed heterozygous female, who may be mildly affected or unaffected — the best natural evidence that partial canonical restoration is clinically meaningful. Not applicable to hemizygous males.
products.domain_consequence: None — wild-type coding sequence, all domains intact.
products.rescue_evidence: CDKL5-specific: an unreviewed 2025 preprint titled 'Epigenetic Reactivation of CDKL5 Rescues CDKL5 Deficiency Disorder' exists; full text could not be retrieved, so no numbers are claimed. Cross-target precedent only: an Xist ASO plus a DNA-methylation inhibitor achieved 30,000-fold MECP2 upregulation from Xi in cultured cells with selective Xi reactivation in vivo.
products.why: Ideal product and an exact natural-human proof of concept in skewed females, but genome-wide Xi reactivation is non-selective, the CDKL5-specific evidence is an unretrievable preprint, and it excludes males.

findings.claim: An Xist ASO combined with a DNA methyltransferase inhibitor achieved 30,000-fold MECP2 upregulation from the inactive X in cultured cells; CDKL5 syndrome is named as a target class for this strategy.
A 2025 preprint reports epigenetic reactivation of CDKL5 rescuing CDD; content not retrievable.
Hemizygous males are most likely severely affected, limiting any Xi-directed product to females.

products.skip: P3 — modulation of the in-frame 41-aa cassette exon 16b/exon 17 (hCDKL5_2, ~10% of brain transcripts)
products.natural_human_equivalent: Both resulting proteins occur naturally in human brain: the canonical 960-aa form and the exon-16b-containing form with 41 extra in-frame residues in the C-terminal half. Both are present in unaffected individuals; no phenotype is attached to the isoform ratio.
products.domain_consequence: Insertion/removal of 41 in-frame residues in the C-terminal regulatory half, downstream of the kinase domain (13-297). No domain is destroyed or fused out of frame.
products.rescue_evidence: None found. No study has modulated exon 16b with an oligonucleotide or shown that the ratio affects CDKL5 activity. Searches: PubMed 'CDKL5 exon 16b', web '"CDKL5" "exon 16b" splicing isoform'.
products.why: The exon is in-frame and not NMD-coupled, so redirecting it reshuffles isoform identity without increasing total productive CDKL5 output — it does not address the dosage deficit.

findings.claim: CDKL5 exon 16b (exon 17 in alternate nomenclature) inserts 41 in-frame residues in the C-terminal half, is brain-specific and highly conserved, and comprises roughly 10% of brain transcripts.
hCDKL5_2, containing this alternative exon, is expressed only at low levels in developing and adult brain.

products.skip: P7 — COMPARATOR (larger change): a protein truncated in the distal C-terminus, i.e. terminating after aa 781, the product an ASO would yield if it bypassed a late premature stop
products.natural_human_equivalent: Directly observed and well characterised: the 'late truncating (after aa781)' CDD variant group. These individuals retain kinase activity and most of the C-terminal region and attain milestones more often — HR 1.72 (95% CI 1.00-2.95) for independent sitting and HR 2.73 (95% CI 1.17-6.35) for independent walking versus other groups. p.Arg970* in the last exon has been reported with late-onset, milder seizure disorder, and variation beyond codon 938 has been argued to be of minor or no significance.
products.domain_consequence: Kinase domain 13-297, ATP site and catalytic D135 fully retained; the distal C-terminus (roughly aa 782 to the 960-aa brain terminus) is lost, removing the C-terminal nuclear localisation/export region that controls CDKL5 subcellular distribution.
products.rescue_evidence: No engineered or therapeutic rescue with this product found. Evidence is human natural-history only (milestone hazard ratios above). Searches: PubMed 'CDKL5 C-terminal deletion kinase activity localization' (0 hits), web late-truncating genotype-phenotype.
products.why: Human data show this truncated protein confers a measurably milder motor/communication course, but these individuals still have CDD with refractory epilepsy — it is a partial product, not a normal one, and one retrieved source argues the opposite severity direction.

findings.claim: Late truncating CDKL5 variants after aa781 'maintain the kinase activity and a large portion of the C-terminal region'; late truncation gave HR 1.72 for independent sitting and HR 2.73 for walking by age 6.

Females with truncating mutations after aa781 attained gross motor, hand function and communication milestones more often than other variant groups; a conflicting report claims C-terminal truncations are more severe.
A p.Arg970X variant in the last CDKL5 exon was associated with a late-onset seizure disorder.
GeneReviews states nonsense alterations throughout the protein appear equally severe, with only terminal-region truncations possibly less severe.

products.skip: P8 — COMPARATOR (largest change): a kinase-domain-only product truncated between aa 172 and aa 781, losing the whole C-terminal region
products.natural_human_equivalent: Observed as the aa172-781 truncating variant group: nonsense/frameshift alleles that preserve kinase activity but delete the C-terminal region. This group is associated with reduced likelihood of independent sitting and walking — i.e. classic severe CDD.
products.domain_consequence: Kinase domain 13-297 retained but the entire C-terminal regulatory region (~aa 298/782 onward to 960), including the NLS/NES sequences governing nuclear-cytoplasmic distribution, is removed.
products.rescue_evidence: None — this is the disease state, not a rescue. No study shows benefit of expressing a C-terminally truncated CDKL5.
products.why: Catalytic competence without the C-terminal regulatory region is exactly the configuration seen in severely affected patients, so frame restoration here would not be product quality.

findings.claim: Truncating variants between aa172 and aa781 cause loss of the C-terminal region while maintaining kinase activity, and reduced the likelihood of achieving independent sitting and walking.
The CDKL5 C-terminus contains the NLS and NES sequences controlling localisation; the N-terminal kinase domain carries the ATP site, active site and TEY motif.

products.skip: P6 — no exon skipped; allele-selective gapmer knockdown of a mutant CDKL5 transcript, wild-type spared
products.natural_human_equivalent: None found. CDD is established as a loss-of-function/haploinsufficiency disorder; no dominant-negative CDKL5 allele was named in this brief, and no retrieved source documents a truncated CDKL5 protein poisoning wild-type function. GeneReviews notes gain-of-function missense and duplications give a different, often milder presentation — not a degradation target.
products.domain_consequence: Not applicable — no protein product is generated by this strategy; the therapeutic output is simply unchanged wild-type protein from the other allele.
products.rescue_evidence: None found. Searches: PubMed/web CDKL5 dominant negative, allele-selective knockdown. No CDKL5 allele-selective ASO reported.
products.why: With no named dominant-negative allele, silencing an already non-functional transcript adds no CDKL5 protein and cannot correct a dosage deficit.

findings.claim: Loss of function is the primary disease mechanism in CDKL5 deficiency disorder; duplications and gain-of-function missense variants cause a different, often milder phenotype.
CDKL5 duplication carriers (7 families) showed autism, developmental delay, hyperactivity and macrocephaly without epilepsy — an overexpression ceiling for any upregulation product.

ranking_rationale: P2 > P1 > P4 > P5 > P9 > P7 > P3 > P8 > P6. P1/P2 yield the unmodified canonical 960-aa brain protein from a healthy allele — the only outcomes with no domain cost — and P2's non-productive event is documented in human brain RNA-seq, not just a data-free patent. P4 has the only quantitative CDKL5 rescue but serves one variant subgroup. Truncated products (P7/P8) remain disease proteins.
